text:
Iris: Quick calibration cheat-card + training/budget tagging for goals. Tiny pack you can paste into goals and 1:1s.

Tom: yes please. managers always forget to flag paid training.

Iris: Rules first: 1) One objective max. 2) 1-2 measurable KRs. 3) If training/headcount required tag with [budget-request]. HR triages those.

Jenna: can we have a 1-line calibration row format for the spreadsheet?

Iris: Use this exact one-line row: "Impact: H/M/L | Confidence: 0-100% | Effort: low/med/high | Dependency: <tag> | Budget: [budget-request or none]" Example: "High | 70% | med | payments-dep | none"

people-ops-bot: Note: if Budget contains [budget-request], HR will contact the owner within 3 business days.

Iris: Pasteable one-line objective templates (pick one):
- Delivery: "Objective: Increase [metric] from [baseline] to [target] to improve [customer outcome]. Owner: [name] [dependency-tag] [budget-tag]"
- Career: "Objective: Develop [skill] by leading [activity]; mentor 1 peer (#career). Owner: [name] [budget-tag]"

Tom: Any micro-feedback to ask peers for quick signals?

Iris: Yes, three-line peer prompt: 1) One specific result I noticed. 2) One way they helped me. 3) One skill to grow next quarter. Keep answers <3 lines.

Arman: How should hiring-linked deliverables be phrased for JDs?

Iris: Include a 90-day deliverable: "90-day key deliverable: Make measurable progress on [OKR one-liner]. Signals: shipped PRs, stakeholder notes, dashboard link." Helps interviewers assess impact fit.

Jenna: Mid-quarter pivot script? managers freeze up when changing KRs.

Iris: Two-liner: "Context changed because [reason]. Proposed change: [new KR one-liner]. I recommend we adopt this to maximize customer impact; approve?"

people-ops-bot: Reminder: quarterly goal window opens Monday. Use the one-line templates to speed review.

Tom: copying into my 1:1 template now, thanks Iris.
